review.notes: Real joke with a compressed image: the burpee (down, up) versus a bin lid, and the raccoon loses. Self-deprecating, species-specific, no target but Rickie.

text: I tried to demonstrate a burpee once. The bin lid won.

review.notes: Turn is genuine - two lazy activities reframed as 'a full schedule'. Dry, warm, in voice, gettable at nine.

text: People ask what I do on rest days. Mostly I think about snacks and look thoughtful. It's a full schedule.

review.notes: Subverts 'personal best' with a deliberately tiny one and then refuses to be embarrassed about it. On-brand without being a slogan, because the pride is the joke.

text: My personal best at anything is 'showed up twice in a row'. I'm very proud of it.

review.notes: Two-part setup with a real punchline in 'I'm working on one of those' - the humour is entirely at the raccoon's expense. Bins are character, not a health suggestion.

text: Raccoon fact: we have extremely good hands and absolutely no self-control around a bin. I'm working on one of those.

review.notes: Rule-of-three subversion of a slogan every reader has heard; 'biscuit' is the payoff. No weight or diet framing - a biscuit is a reward, not a calorie note.

text: I don't do 'no pain no gain'. I do 'mild inconvenience, some gain, biscuit'.

review.notes: Strongest of the deflection lines: 'a raccoon with opinions' is a fresh self-label and 'there's overlap' is a real dry beat rather than an affirmation.

text: Somebody asked if I'm a personal trainer. I'm a raccoon with opinions. There's overlap.

review.notes: Opens with a verbatim fitness-industry aphorism ('the best exercise is the one you'll actually do') and closes on the affirmation 'Both count'. The complaining beat in the middle is the only original part - rebuild the line around it and drop the borrowed opener.

text: The best exercise is the one you'll actually do. The second best is the one you'll do while complaining. Both count.

review.notes: Best Rickie line in the packet. Two sentences, no wasted word, and the joke is the gap between the achievement and the bragging. Entirely self-deprecating.

text: I once did twelve push-ups. I've been mentioning it for two years.

review.notes: 'The sigh is load-bearing' is a real pun (structural load / training load). Mild reservation that 'load-bearing' is architectural vocabulary a nine-year-old may not hold, but it is inferable from the words themselves and the line still reads warm without the pun.

text: My warm-up is a stretch and a sigh. The sigh is load-bearing.

review.notes: Original raccoon-specific premise with a two-stage punchline ('unconvinced' then 'slightly disappointed'). Appearance humour, but strictly about his own face, which the rubric permits.

text: I'm told the mask isn't a disguise, it's just my face. I remain unconvinced and slightly disappointed.

review.notes: Punchline is funny but the premise is wrong for the slot: it addresses a reader who has not moved and tells them that is fine. This line is served after a completed workout, so the setup does not apply, and as written it lightly rewards not moving. Re-aim the meta joke at a reader who has just finished.

text: If you're reading this instead of moving, that's fine. I'm reading it too and I wrote it.

review.notes: No joke and no Rickie voice - this is the product's own value proposition ('five minutes still counts') stated flatly in three beats. As the day's single reward it is marketing copy, not a reward. Needs an actual turn or it should be a coaching line elsewhere in the app.

text: Five minutes is not a small workout. It's a workout. The five is just how long it took.

review.notes: 'Never regretted a walk' is a common sentiment, but the second sentence genuinely earns it - the swerve to regretting other things at speed is original and dry.

text: I have never once regretted a walk. I've regretted plenty of other things at speed.

review.notes: A poster aphorism with nothing funny, nothing self-deprecating and no raccoon in it. True and warm, but interchangeable with any generic fitness app's copy - it fails the 'inoffensive is not the bar' test for the reward slot.

text: Rest days aren't days off. They're the bit where the work turns into something.

review.notes: Good line in isolation, but it is the same joke shape as SF-RCK-000006 (somebody assigns Rickie a title; Rickie counters with a wry self-label) and the face gag overlaps SF-RCK-000010. Two of fifteen asides on one template is template fatigue - keep 000006 and rework this one, or space them far apart in the rotation.

text: Somebody called me a mascot. I prefer 'colleague with an unusual face'.
